Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal ran a quick review of the MSA and Order Form and pushed back on a few items related to model outputs and the feedback/training license. I've attached our redlines (MedTech_MSA_redline_v2.docx and OrderForm_MedTech_redline.xlsx). High level:

- We need explicit ownership of output (language that states we own the outputs generated from our prompts).
- We want an explicit carveout that prevents Redwood from using any of our customer-provided data or outputs for model training.
- Procurement wants a limited feedback license that allows Redwood to use aggregated telemetry for diagnostics but not to improve models.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a strict training prohibition and a narrow telemetry-only feedback license? Procurement would like to get this sorted this week so we can move to signature.

Sabrina — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Looping in Steph (legal) and Laura (Product) to weigh in on non-starters vs. acceptable language. A couple quick clarifications from our side before legal digs in:

- When you say “own the outputs,” is MedTechCo asking for an exclusive IP assignment of generated text and embeddings, or a broad customer ownership + right to use internally? We commonly grant output ownership to customers but need a limited rights grant back for debugging and to operate the service.
- On training prohibition: do you mean a complete ban on using any customer inputs/outputs to train Redwood models (including aggregated/anonymous signals), or a ban on model-weights/LLM training but allow telemetry for feature fixes?
- For the feedback license, can you share an example of acceptable language (procurement sometimes provides one-liners)?

Internal plan: Steph will propose redline language for a telemetry-only feedback license (anonymized, aggregate, only for service reliability) and carve out training for commercial model improvements. Laura will comment on operational implications (retention windows, KV cache). I’ll coordinate a 30-min alignment call with your team for tomorrow afternoon if that works.

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: RE: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (output use, training/feedback)

Karthik / Laura — reviewed MedTech's redlines. Short summary of legal position and suggested compromise language to keep deal moving:

1) Output ownership
- Suggested stance: Redwood grants the customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to the Outputs (customer prompt + generated content) for the customer’s internal business purposes and to distribute to its customers. We should resist assignment of underlying model IP or derivative claims that could constrain Redwood’s model development.
- Draft line: "Customer shall own the Outputs. Redwood retains all rights in the underlying models and model weights, and no transfer of Redwood's proprietary model IP is intended by this agreement."

2) Training prohibition
- We can accept a prohibition on using customer-provided data or Outputs to train Redwood's production models, with a carveout for operationally necessary telemetry (see below). The prohibition should be timeboxed (e.g., cannot use for training without customer consent for X years) or scoped to exclude anonymized, aggregated service telemetry.
- Draft line: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to retrain or otherwise improve Redwood's models for commercial purposes without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Feedback/telemetry license
- Recommend offering a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use de-identified, aggregated Feedback solely for service diagnostics, security, and stability improvements — expressly excluding those materials from being used to update model weights for commercial models.
- Draft line: "Customer grants Redwood a limited license to use de-identified, aggregated Feedback for the sole purpose of service operation, diagnostics, and security, provided such Feedback cannot be traced to Customer and shall not be used to update model parameters for commercial model releases."

4) Retention and audit
- Product asks for a short retention window for telemetry (e.g., 90 days for detailed logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics) and an audit metric for data deletion. Laura, please confirm operational feasibility.

Next steps: I can produce a redline that incorporates the above. If the customer insists on absolute, perpetual bans that prevent us from operating/improving, we should escalate to execs for waiver.

Attaching: proposed_redline_text.txt (annotated excerpts) — will convert to doc if we decide to send.

— Steph
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (output use, training/feedback)

Sabrina — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity from Procurement. We've reviewed with Legal and Product and propose the following approach to get to signature quickly:

1) Output ownership: Redwood is comfortable granting Customer ownership of Outputs for Customer's internal use and redistribution to its end customers. We will add explicit language clarifying Redwood retains ownership of model code, weights, and any derivative improvements to the model.

2) Training prohibition: Redwood can agree not to use Customer Content or Outputs to retrain or improve commercial model weights without prior written consent. However, we need a narrow exception for de-identified, aggregated telemetry used only for diagnostics and reliability. We propose the draft language below (taken from our legal team):

-- Proposed: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to retrain or otherwise improve Redwood's commercially deployed model weights without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may, however, collect de-identified, aggregated service telemetry for the limited purpose of diagnosing and resolving service issues, provided such telemetry cannot be reverse-engineered to re-create Customer Content or Outputs."

3) Feedback license: Redwood will accept a limited feedback license for de-identified, aggregated data for diagnostics/security only; explicitly excluded: use to update model parameters for product improvement.

4) Retention: Proposed operational retention window: 90 days for detailed logs (error traces, request/response pairs), 365 days for aggregated metrics. If this is a blocker, propose an alternatives call.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow (Sun 5/16) at 11:00 AM PT to confirm language and allow us to issue clean docs for signature? If so, we'll share a DocuSign/clean MSA and a redlined version for your legal to confirm.

Attachments: (internal) proposed_redline_text.txt
Related links: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEF123456, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMedTech-MSA

Best,
Karthik
